paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.

model_annotations.English:
The figure presents two line plots illustrating the distribution of important feed-forward network (FFN) value neurons across layers in the Llama3-8B model, in relation to confusion points induced by Chinese prompts. Both plots share a common x-axis labeled "layer" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 35, marked with tick labels at regular intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, ..., 35). The y-axis in both plots is labeled "count" and represents the number of important neurons, using a linear scale; in plot (a) the range is 0 to 100 with tick marks every 20 units, while in plot (b) the range is 0 to 175 with tick marks every 25 units. 

Plot (a), titled "Individual Case," displays a single blue line with circular markers representing the top 300 most important FFN neurons for a single Chinese prompt from the Aya dataset. The count starts near 0 for layers 0 through 24, remains relatively flat with minor fluctuations, and then rises sharply starting at layer 25, reaching approximately 25 at layer 28, 75 at layer 30, and 100 at layer 31. 

Plot (b), titled "Aggregated Neuron Scores," shows a single green line with circular markers representing the aggregated neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in the Aya dataset. The count is near 0 for layers 0 through 26, remains flat with negligible values (mostly 0 or 1), and then increases steeply from layer 27, reaching approximately 15 at layer 28, 50 at layer 29, 100 at layer 30, and exceeding 150 by layer 31.
model_annotations.German: The figure presents two line plots, (a) and (b), both illustrating the distribution of important neurons associated with confusion points in the Llama3-8B model, with the x-axis representing the model layer (ranging from 0 to 35 in both plots, with tick marks at intervals of 5) and the y-axis representing the count of important neurons (in plot (a) ranging from 0 to 100, and in plot (b) from 0 to 175, both on linear scales). In plot (a), titled "Individual Case," a blue line with circular markers represents the count of the top 300 most important FFN value neurons for a single Chinese prompt from the Aya dataset. The count remains near zero for layers 0 through 25, then increases to approximately 20 at layer 26, dips slightly to around 10 at layer 27, rises to about 25 at layer 28, then climbs sharply to 80 at layer 30 and reaches 100 at layer 32. In plot (b), titled "Aggregated Neuron Scores," a green line with circular markers shows the aggregated count of important FFN value neurons across all Chinese test samples in Aya. The count remains near zero for layers 0 through 25, then increases to approximately 5 at layer 26, rises to about 10 at layer 27, increases further to around 20 at layer 28, then jumps to 50 at layer 29, and sharply rises to 150 at layer 30 and 175 at layer 32. Both plots show a similar trend of low neuron importance in early layers and a sharp increase in the final layers, with plot (b) exhibiting higher overall counts due to aggregation.
